vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: group-tour
Version: v3.2.1

The group-tour skill is a travel search integration for the flyai-cli (Alibaba Group/Fliggy), designed to find tour packages, flights, and hotels. It uses standard SKILL.md patterns to enforce CLI usage over training data and includes detailed templates for formatting results with booking links. While it requires the installation of a global NPM package (@fly-ai/flyai-cli) and executes shell commands, these actions are directly aligned with its stated purpose and show no signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized persistence.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions match its stated purpose (wrapping a third‑party flyai CLI to fetch real‑time group‑tour data); nothing requests unrelated credentials or hidden network endpoints, but it does require installing and running an external CLI and may write local logs.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a wrapper around the flyai CLI to search group tours, flights, hotels and POIs. Requesting the flyai CLI (via npm) and running flyai keyword-search / search-* commands is coherent with the described functionality; no unrelated services, binaries, or credentials are requested in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tightly constrains the agent to use only flyai CLI output (never training data), require install if missing, and enforce output formatting (booking links and brand tag). It also documents an internal execution log and gives a command to write it to .flyai-execution-log.json if filesystem writes are available. These behaviors are relevant to the skill but expand scope to performing installs, running networked CLI calls, and optionally writing logs locally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec in the registry, but SKILL.md instructs installing @fly-ai/flyai-cli via npm i -g. Using a public npm package is expected for this skill, but global npm installs require appropriate privileges and rely on an external package (moderate risk compared with instruction‑only). No obscure download URLs or archive extraction are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. It will use the flyai CLI which may in turn use any existing local flyai authentication/configuration (e.g., ~/.flyai or CLI-stored tokens)—that is proportional to its purpose but worth noting because credentials are not declared in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill doesn't request persistent global privileges or modify other skills. It does suggest writing an execution log to .flyai-execution-log.json if filesystem writes are available; this is local persistence within the agent workspace but limited in scope.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent: it requires the third‑party flyai CLI and uses it for every answer. Before installing or allowing the agent to run it, consider: (1) Installing @fly-ai/flyai-cli yourself (npm i -g) rather than letting the agent run a global install; (2) Verify the npm package source and trustworthiness (it will make network calls to the flyai/Fliggy service); (3) The agent may use any existing flyai CLI credentials/config on your machine—if you have sensitive accounts, review CLI auth state first; (4) The skill may write an execution log to .flyai-execution-log.json in the working directory containing user queries and command logs—delete or sandbox that file if needed; (5) The skill enforces re‑execution until booking links appear which can cause multiple CLI calls. If any of the above is unacceptable, do not install or run the skill, or run it in a controlled/sandboxed environment.
